verses.51:5: My righteousness draws near quickly, and My salvation also will go out like a light, and in My arm nations will hope; islands will wait for Me, and in My arm they will hope.
verses.51:6: Lift up your eyes to heaven, and look at the earth below; for heaven was made firm like smoke, and the earth will grow old like a garment, and the inhabitants will die just like these things, but My salvation will be forever, and My righteousness will never fail.
verses.51:7: Listen to Me, you who know justice, a people in whose heart is My law: do not fear the reproach of men, and do not be defeated by their contempt.
verses.51:8: For like a garment it will be eaten by time, and like wool it will be eaten by a moth, but My righteousness will be forever, and My salvation for generations of generations.
verses.51:9: Awake, awake, Jerusalem, and put on the strength of your arm; awake as in the beginning of a day, as a generation of eternity.
verses.51:10: Are you not the one who makes the sea desolate, water of the abyss, an abundance? The one who made the depths of the sea a way of crossing for those being rescued
verses.51:11: and those who have been redeemed? For by the Lord they will be brought back, and they will come to Zion with gladness and everlasting exultation; for upon their head is praise, and gladness will overtake them; pain and grief and sighing have fled away.
verses.51:12: I am, I am the One who comforts you; know who you are, that you were afraid of mortal man and of a son of man, who withered like grass.
verses.51:13: And you forgot God who made you, who made heaven and laid the foundation of the earth; and you feared continually all the days the face of the wrath of the one who afflicts you, for how he plotted to take you away; and now where is the wrath of the one who afflicts you?
verses.51:14: For when you are being saved, it will not stand nor delay;
verses.51:15: for I am your God, who stirs up the sea and makes its waves roar; the Lord Sabaoth is My name.
verses.51:16: I will put My words into your mouth, and under the shadow of My hand I will shelter you, by which I established heaven and laid the foundation of the earth; and He will say to Zion, "You are My people."
verses.51:17: Awake, awake, rise up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the Lord the cup of His wrath; for the cup of downfall, the goblet of wrath, you drank up and emptied out,
verses.51:18: and there was no one comforting you from among all your children whom you bore, and there was no one taking hold of your hand, not even from among all your sons whom you raised up.
verses.51:19: These two things are opposed to you: who will grieve with you? Ruin and destruction, famine and sword; who will comfort you?
verses.51:20: Your sons, who are at a loss, who sleep at the head of every exit like a half-boiled beet, who are full of the wrath of the Lord, exhausted by the Lord God.
verses.51:21: Therefore listen, you who have been humbled and who are drunk, not from wine.
verses.51:22: Thus says the Lord God, who judges His people: "Look, I have taken out of your hand the cup of downfall, the goblet of My wrath, and you will not again drink it;
verses.51:23: and I will give it into the hands of those who wronged you, those who humbled you, who said to your soul, 'Bow down, so that we may pass over,' and you made your middle even with the ground outside for those passing by."
verses.52:1: Awake, awake, Zion; put on your strength, Zion, and you, put on your glory, Jerusalem, the holy city; no longer will anyone uncircumcised and unclean pass through you again.
verses.52:2: Shake off the dust and rise up, sit down, Jerusalem; loose the bond of your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
verses.52:3: For thus says the Lord: "You were sold for nothing, and not with silver will you be redeemed."
verses.52:4: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: "To Egypt My people went down at first to sojourn there, and to the Assyrians they were led by force;
verses.52:5: and now why are you here?" Thus says the Lord: "Because My people was taken for nothing, marvel and wail." Thus says the Lord: "Because of you My name is continually blasphemed among the nations.
verses.52:6: Therefore My people will know My name in that day, that I Myself am the One who speaks; I am present like a season upon the mountains,
verses.52:7: like the feet of one bringing good news, a report of peace, like one bringing good news of good things, for I will make your salvation heard, saying to Zion, 'Your God will reign.'"
verses.52:8: For the voice of those who guard you has been lifted up, and with the voice together they will rejoice; for eyes will look to eyes when the Lord has mercy on Zion.
verses.52:9: Let the desolate places of Jerusalem break forth together into gladness, for the Lord has had mercy on her and has rescued Jerusalem.
verses.52:10: And the Lord will reveal His holy arm before all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation from our God.
verses.52:11: Depart, depart, go out from there and touch nothing unclean; go out from the midst of her, separate yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the Lord;
verses.52:12: for not with turmoil will you go out, nor will you go in flight; for the Lord will go first before you, and the God of Israel, the One who gathers you together.
verses.52:13: Look, My servant will understand, and he will be lifted up and glorified exceedingly.
verses.52:14: Just as many will be astonished at you, so your appearance will be without glory from men, and your glory from men.
verses.52:15: So many nations will marvel at him, and kings will shut their mouth; for those to whom it was not announced concerning him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.
verses.53:1: Lord, who believed our message? And to whom was the arm of the Lord revealed?
verses.53:2: We announced before him as a child, as a root in thirsty ground; he has no form or glory. And we saw him, and he had no form or beauty;
verses.53:3: but his form was without honor and failing beyond the sons of men; he was a man in plague and knowing how to bear sickness, because his face has been turned away; he was dishonored and not reckoned.
verses.53:4: This one bears our sins and suffers anguish for us, and we reckoned him to be in pain and in plague and in affliction.
verses.53:5: But he was wounded because of our sins, and he has been made sick because of our lawless deeds; the discipline of our peace was upon him; by his bruise we were healed.
verses.53:6: All of us went astray like sheep; each man went astray in his own way; and the Lord handed him over to our sins.
verses.53:7: And he, because he has been afflicted, does not open his mouth; like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before the one shearing it is silent, so he does not open his mouth.
verses.53:8: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away; who will describe his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth; because of the lawless deeds of My people he was led to death.
verses.53:9: And I will give the wicked in exchange for his burial, and the rich in exchange for his death; because he did no lawlessness, nor was there deceit in his mouth.
verses.53:10: And the Lord desires to cleanse him from the plague. If you give an offering for sin, our soul will see a long-lived seed.
verses.53:11: And the Lord desires to take away from the pain of his soul, to show him light and to form him with understanding, to justify a righteous one who serves many well; and he himself will bear their sins.
verses.53:12: Therefore he will inherit many, and he will divide the spoils of the strong, because his soul was handed over to death, and he was reckoned among the lawless; and he himself bore the sins of many, and because of their lawless deeds he was handed over.
verses.54:1: Rejoice, barren one, you who do not bear; break forth and shout, you who are not in labor, for the children of the desolate one are many, more than of the one who has the husband, for the Lord said.
verses.54:2: Widen the place of your tent and of your curtains; fasten it, do not spare; lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes,
verses.54:3: spread out further to the right and to the left; and your seed will inherit nations, and you will resettle desolated cities.
verses.54:4: Do not fear because you were put to shame, nor be ashamed because you were reproached; for you will forget everlasting shame, and the reproach of your widowhood you will never remember.
verses.54:5: For the Lord is the One who makes you, the Lord Sabaoth is His name; and the One who rescued you will Himself be called the God of Israel by all the earth.
verses.54:6: Not like a forsaken and fainthearted woman has the Lord called you, nor like a woman hated from youth, your God said.
verses.54:7: For a little time I forsook you, and with great mercy I will have mercy on you;
verses.54:8: in a little wrath I turned My face away from you, and with everlasting mercy I will have mercy on you, said the Lord who rescued you.
verses.54:9: From the water in the time of Noah this is to Me, just as I swore to him at that time, to the earth, not to be angry against you anymore, nor that in threatening you the mountains will be removed,
verses.54:10: nor will your hills be moved; so neither will the mercy from Me to you fail, nor will the covenant of your peace ever be removed; for he said, "Merciful to you, Lord."
verses.54:11: Humbled and unsettled, you were not comforted; look, I am preparing for you carbuncle as your stone, and sapphire as your foundations,
verses.54:12: and I will make your battlements jasper, and your gates stones of crystal, and your surrounding wall choice stones,
verses.54:13: and all your sons taught by God, and your children in great peace.
verses.54:14: And in righteousness you will be built; keep away from unrighteousness, and you will not fear, and trembling will not draw near to you.
verses.54:15: Look, proselytes will come to you through Me, and they will sojourn with you and flee to you for refuge.
verses.54:16: Look, I created you, not like a smith blowing on coals and bringing out an instrument for work; but I created you not for destruction, to ruin.
verses.54:17: No instrument fashioned against you will I prosper; and every voice that rises against you for judgment, all of them you will defeat, and those guilty against you will be in it. There is an inheritance for those who serve the Lord, and you will be righteous to Me, says the Lord.
verses.55:1: You who are thirsty, go to the water, and all you who have no silver, go, buy, and eat wine and fat without silver and price.
verses.55:2: Why do you spend silver, and your labor not for satisfaction? And you will eat good things, and your soul will delight in good things.
verses.55:3: Pay attention with your ears and follow My ways; listen to Me, and your soul will live in good things, and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful holy things of David.
verses.55:4: Look, I have given him as a testimony among nations, a ruler and commander for nations.
verses.55:5: Nations that do not know you will call upon you, and peoples who are not acquainted with you will flee to you for refuge, because of the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you.
verses.55:6: Seek the Lord, and upon finding Him, call upon Him; and whenever He draws near to you,
verses.55:7: let the ungodly one forsake his ways, and a lawless man his plans, and let him turn back to the Lord, and he will be shown mercy, for He will greatly forgive your sins.
verses.55:8: "For My plans are not like your plans, nor like your ways are My ways," says the Lord,
verses.55:9: "but as far as heaven is from the earth, so far is My way from your ways, and your thoughts from My thought.
verses.55:10: For as the rain or snow comes down from heaven, and does not return until it drenches the earth, and brings forth and sprouts, and gives seed to the sower and bread for food,
verses.55:11: so will My word be that goes out from My mouth: it will not return until all that I willed is accomplished, and I will prosper your ways and My commands."
verses.55:12: For in gladness you will go out, and in joy you will be taught; for the mountains and the hills will leap up as they welcome you in joy, and all the trees of the field will clap with their branches,
verses.55:13: and instead of the thornbush a cypress will come up, and instead of the fleabane a myrtle will come up; and the Lord will be for a name and for an everlasting sign, and will not fail.
verses.56:1: Thus says the Lord: "Keep justice and do righteousness, for My salvation has drawn near to come, and My mercy to be revealed.
verses.56:2: Blessed is the man who does these things, and the person who holds fast to them, and keeps the Sabbaths so as not to profane them, and guards his hands from doing unrighteous things."
verses.56:3: Do not let the foreigner who joins himself to the Lord say, "Surely the Lord will separate me from His people"; and do not let the eunuch say, "I am a dry tree."
verses.56:4: Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs: "All who keep My Sabbaths and choose the things that I desire and hold fast to My covenant,
verses.56:5: I will give them in My house and in My wall a renowned place, better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it will not fail.
verses.56:6: And as for the foreigners who join themselves to the Lord to serve Him, and to love the name of the Lord so as to be male and female servants to Him, and all who keep My Sabbaths so as not to profane them and hold fast to My covenant,
verses.56:7: I will bring them into My holy mountain, and I will make them glad in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be acceptable upon My altar. For My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations,"
verses.56:8: said the Lord who gathers the dispersed of Israel, "I will gather a gathering to him."
verses.56:9: All you wild beasts, come, eat, all you beasts of the forest.
verses.56:10: See that they have all been blinded; they have not known; mute dogs, they will not be able to bark, dreaming of a bed, loving to slumber.
verses.56:11: And the dogs are shameless in soul, not knowing satisfaction; and they are wicked, not knowing understanding; all have followed their own ways, each one according to what is his own.
verses.57:1: See how the righteous one has perished, and no one takes it to heart, and righteous men are taken away, and no one considers. For from the face of unrighteousness the righteous one has been taken away;
verses.57:2: his burial will be in peace; he has been taken away from the midst.
verses.57:3: But you, come near here, lawless sons, seed of adulterers and a prostitute;
verses.57:4: in whom did you delight? And against whom did you open your mouth? And against whom did you let loose your tongue? Are you not children of destruction, lawless seed?
verses.57:5: Those who entreat the idols under leafy trees, slaughtering their children in the valleys in the midst of the rocks.
verses.57:6: That is your portion, this is your lot, and to those you poured out drink offerings, and to these you offered up sacrifices; over these things, then, will I not be angry?
verses.57:7: Upon a high and lofty mountain, there is your bed, and there you brought up sacrifices;
verses.57:8: and behind the posts of your door you placed your memorials; you thought that if you turned away from Me, you would have something more; you loved those who sleep with you,
verses.57:9: and you multiplied your prostitution with them, and you made those far from you many, and you sent envoys beyond your borders, and you were brought low as far as Hades.
verses.57:10: By your many journeys you grew weary, and you did not say, "I will stop," growing strong because you did these things; because of this you yourself did not entreat Me.
verses.57:11: Whom did you dread and fear, that you lied to Me and did not remember, nor did you take Me into your mind or into your heart? And I, seeing you, look past you, and you did not fear Me.
verses.57:12: And I will declare your righteousness and your evil deeds, which will not benefit you;
verses.57:13: when you cry out, let them rescue you in your affliction; for wind will take all these, and a storm will carry them away. But those who hold fast to Me will possess the land, and will inherit My holy mountain,
verses.57:14: and they will say, "Clear ways from before him, and take away stumbling blocks from the way of My people."
verses.57:15: Thus says the Most High in the high places, inhabiting eternity, Holy in the holy places is His name, Most High resting in the holy places, and giving patience to the fainthearted, and giving life to those crushed in heart:
verses.57:16: "I will not take vengeance on you forever, nor will I be angry with you continually; for a spirit will go forth from Me, and I Myself made every breath.
verses.57:17: Because of sin I grieved him for a little while, and I struck him and turned My face away from him; and he was grieved, and went downcast in his ways.
verses.57:18: I have seen his ways, and I healed him and comforted him, and I gave him true comfort,
verses.57:19: peace upon peace to those who are far off and to those who are near." And the Lord said, "I will heal them";
verses.57:20: but the unrighteous will be tossed like waves and will not be able to rest.
verses.57:21: "There is no rejoicing," said God, "for the ungodly."
verses.58:1: Cry out with strength and do not spare; like a trumpet, lift up your voice, and announce to My people their sinful deeds, and to the house of Jacob their lawless deeds.
verses.58:2: Day after day they seek Me and desire to know My ways, like a people that has practiced righteousness and has not forsaken the justice of its God; now they ask Me for a righteous judgment, and they desire to draw near to God,
verses.58:3: saying, "Why did we fast, and You did not see? We humbled our souls, and You did not know?" For in the days of your fasts you find your wishes, and you goad all those subject to you.
verses.58:4: If you fast for disputes and fights and strike a humble person with fists, why do you fast for Me as today, for your voice to be heard in an outcry?
verses.58:5: I did not choose this fast, nor a day for a person to humble his soul; not even if you bend your neck like a ring, and spread sackcloth and ashes under yourself, not even so will you call it an acceptable fast.
verses.58:6: I did not choose such a fast, says the Lord; rather, loose every bond of injustice, untie the knots of coercive transactions, send away those who are crushed in release, and tear apart every unjust contract.
verses.58:7: Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; if you see someone who is naked, clothe him, and you shall not disregard the relatives of your seed.
verses.58:8: Then your light will break forth early, and your healings will quickly rise up, and your righteousness will go ahead before you, and the glory of God will enfold you.
verses.58:9: Then you will cry out, and God will listen to you; while you are still speaking, He will say, "Look, I am here." If you remove from yourself the bond and the pointing of the hand and a word of grumbling,
verses.58:10: and give the hungry the bread from your soul, and satisfy a humbled soul, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will be like midday,
verses.58:11: and your God will be with you continually; and you will be satisfied just as your soul desires, and your bones will be fattened, and they will be like a saturated garden and like a spring whose water has not failed.
verses.58:12: And your age-old desolate places will be built, and your foundations will be eternal for generations of generations; and you will be called "Builder of Fences," and you will cause your paths in the midst to cease.
verses.58:13: If you turn your foot away from the Sabbath so as not to do your wishes on the holy day, then you will call the Sabbath delightful, holy to God; you will not lift your foot for work, nor speak a word in anger from your mouth,
verses.58:14: and you will trust in the Lord, and He will bring you up upon the good things of the land, and feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.
verses.59:1: Is the hand of the Lord not strong enough to save? Or has His ear grown heavy so as not to listen?
verses.59:2: Rather, your sinful deeds divide between you and God, and because of your sins He turned His face away from you so as not to have mercy.
verses.59:3: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers are in sins; your lips have spoken lawlessness, and your tongue meditates on injustice.
verses.59:4: No one speaks righteous things, nor is there true justice; they trust in futile things and speak empty things, because they conceive trouble and give birth to lawlessness.
verses.59:5: They have broken open eggs of asps, and they weave a spider's web; and the one who is about to eat from their eggs, upon crushing one, found an addled egg, and in it was a basilisk.
verses.59:6: Their web will not become a garment, nor will they clothe themselves from their works; for their works are works of lawlessness.
verses.59:7: And their feet run toward wickedness, swift to shed blood, and their thoughts come from murders; ruin and misery are in their ways,
verses.59:8: and they do not know a way of peace, and there is no justice in their ways; for the paths that they travel are crooked, and they do not know peace.
verses.59:9: Therefore justice has departed from them, and righteousness will never overtake them; while they waited for light, darkness came to them; waiting for brightness, they walked in gloom.
verses.59:10: They will grope for a wall like the blind, and as though having no eyes they will grope; they will fall at midday as at midnight; like those who are dying they will groan,
verses.59:11: like a bear and like a dove they will go together; we waited for justice, and there is none; salvation stands far off from us.
verses.59:12: For our lawlessness is great before You, and our sins have stood against us; for our lawless deeds are within us, and our unjust deeds we have known;
verses.59:13: we acted ungodly and lied, and turned away from behind our God; we spoke unjust things and disobeyed, we were conceiving and devising unjust words from our heart,
verses.59:14: and we drove justice back, and righteousness stands far off; for truth has been consumed in their ways, and they were not able to pass through a straight course.
verses.59:15: And truth has been taken away, and they removed their mind from understanding; and the Lord saw, and it did not please Him, because there was no justice.
verses.59:16: And He saw, and there was no man, and He observed, and there was no one to assist; and He defended them with His arm, and with mercy He sustained Himself.
verses.59:17: And He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and placed a helmet of salvation upon His head, and clothed Himself with a garment of vengeance and His cloak,
verses.59:18: as One about to repay a repayment, a reproach to the adversaries.
verses.59:19: And those from the west will fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the sun the glorious name; for wrath from the Lord will come like a violent river; it will come with fury.
verses.59:20: And the Deliverer will come for the sake of Zion, and He will turn away ungodly deeds from Jacob.
verses.59:21: And this is the covenant for them from Me, said the Lord: My Spirit that is upon you, and the words that I have put into your mouth, will never fail from your mouth and from the mouth of your seed; for the Lord has said, from now and forever.
verses.60:1: Be illuminated, be illuminated, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
verses.60:2: Look, darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness will be upon the nations; but upon you the Lord will appear, and His glory will be seen upon you.
verses.60:3: And kings will walk by your light, and nations by your brightness.
verses.60:4: Lift up your eyes all around and see your children gathered together; all your sons have come from afar, and your daughters will be carried on shoulders.
verses.60:5: Then you will see, and you will fear and be amazed in your heart, because the wealth of the sea and of nations and of peoples will turn to you. And herds of camels will come to you,
verses.60:6: and camels of Midian and Ephah will cover you; all from Sheba will come bringing gold, and they will bring frankincense, and they will proclaim the good news of the salvation of the Lord;
verses.60:7: and all the sheep of Kedar will be gathered together, and rams of Nebaioth will come, and acceptable things will be offered up upon My altar, and the house of My prayer will be glorified.
verses.60:8: Who are these that fly like clouds, and like doves with nestlings to Me?
verses.60:9: For Me the islands have waited, and ships of Tarshish among the first, to bring your children from afar, and their silver and their gold with them, and the holy name of the Lord, and because the Holy One of Israel is glorious.
verses.60:10: And foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will attend you; for because of My wrath I struck you, and because of mercy I loved you.
verses.60:11: And your gates will be opened continually; day and night they will not be shut, to bring in to you the power of nations and their kings being led.
verses.60:12: For the nations and the kings who will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be made utterly desolate.
verses.60:13: And the glory of Lebanon will come to you, with cypress and pine and cedar together, to glorify My holy place.
verses.60:14: And the sons of those who humbled you and provoked you will come to you in fear, and you will be called "City of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel."
verses.60:15: Because you have become forsaken and hated, and there was no one to help, I will make you an eternal exultation, a joy for generations of generations.
verses.60:16: And you will nurse on the milk of nations, and you will eat the wealth of kings, and you will know that I am the Lord who saves you and rescues you, the God of Israel.
verses.60:17: Instead of bronze I will bring you gold, and instead of iron I will bring you silver, and instead of wood I will bring you bronze, and instead of stones, iron. And I will appoint your rulers in peace, and your overseers in righteousness;
verses.60:18: and injustice will no longer be heard in your land, nor ruin nor misery within your borders; rather, your walls will be called "Salvation," and your gates "Carving."
verses.60:19: And the sun will no longer be light by day for you, nor will the rising of the moon illuminate the night for you; rather, the Lord will be an eternal light for you, and God your glory.
verses.60:20: For the sun will not set for you, and the moon will not fail you; for the Lord will be an eternal light for you, and the days of your mourning will be fulfilled.
verses.60:21: And your people will all be righteous; forever they will inherit the land, guarding the planting, the works of His hands, for glory.
verses.60:22: The smallest one will become thousands, and the least one a great nation; I, the Lord, in due time will gather them.
verses.61:1: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He anointed me; He has sent me to announce good news to the poor, to heal those crushed in heart, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind,
verses.61:2: to declare an acceptable year of the Lord and a day of retribution, to comfort all who mourn,
verses.61:3: that to those who mourn in Zion, to them, glory may be given instead of ashes, oil of gladness to those who mourn, a robe of glory instead of a spirit of dejection; and they will be called generations of righteousness, a planting of the Lord for glory.
verses.61:4: And they will build ancient desolate places; those previously laid desolate they will raise up; and they will renew desolate cities, laid desolate for generations.
verses.61:5: And foreigners will come shepherding your sheep, and aliens as plowmen and vinedressers;
verses.61:6: but you will be called priests of the Lord, ministers of God; you will consume the strength of nations, and in their wealth you will be marveled at.
verses.61:7: Thus they will inherit the land a second time, and everlasting gladness will be over their head.
verses.61:8: For I am the Lord who loves righteousness and hates plunder from unrighteousness; and I will give their labor to the righteous, and an everlasting covenant I will make with them.
verses.61:9: And their seed will be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples; everyone who sees them will recognize them, that these are a seed blessed by God,
verses.61:10: and with gladness they will be glad in the Lord. Let my soul exult in the Lord; for He has clothed me with a garment of salvation and a tunic of gladness; He has placed a turban on me as on a bridegroom, and as a bride He has adorned me with ornament.
verses.61:11: And as the earth causes its blossom to grow, and as a garden its seeds, so the Lord, the Lord will cause righteousness and exultation to spring up before all the nations.
verses.62:1: For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not let up, until her righteousness goes forth like light, and My salvation will burn like a torch.
verses.62:2: And nations will see your righteousness, and kings your glory, and one will call you the new name that the Lord will name.
verses.62:3: And you will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a diadem of kingship in the hand of your God.
verses.62:4: And you will no longer be called "Forsaken," and your land will no longer be called "Desolate"; for you will be called "My Delight," and your land "Inhabited," because the Lord has delighted in you, and your land will be settled.
verses.62:5: And as a young man dwells with a virgin, so your sons will dwell; and it will be that in the way a bridegroom will be glad over a bride, so the Lord will be glad over you.
verses.62:6: And upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen all the day and all the night, who continually will not be silent, remembering the Lord.
verses.62:7: For there is no one like you; if He establishes, and makes Jerusalem a boast on the earth.
verses.62:8: The Lord has sworn by His glory and by the strength of His arm: "I will certainly no longer give your grain and food to your enemies, and foreign sons will no longer drink your wine for which you labored;
verses.62:9: but those who gathered them will eat them and praise the Lord, and those who gathered them will drink them in My holy courts."
verses.62:10: Go through My gates, and make a way for My people, and cast the stones out of the way; lift up a signal to the nations.
verses.62:11: For look, the Lord has made it heard to the end of the earth; say to the daughter of Zion, "Look, the Savior has come to you, having His own reward, and His work before His face."
verses.62:12: And one will call them "Holy People, Redeemed by the Lord," but you will be called "Sought-After City" and "Not Forsaken."
verses.63:1: Who is this coming from Edom, with redness of garments from Bozrah? So splendid in a robe, with force, with strength? I declare righteousness and judgment of salvation.
verses.63:2: Why are Your garments red, and Your clothing as from a trodden winepress?
verses.63:3: I am full of a trampled winepress, and of the nations there is no man with Me; and I trampled them in My wrath, and I crushed them like earth, and I brought down their blood.
verses.63:4: For a day of retribution has come upon them, and a year of redemption is here.
verses.63:5: And I looked, and there was no helper; and I observed, and no one was coming to aid; and My arm rescued them, and My wrath stood firm.
verses.63:6: And I trampled them in My anger, and I brought down their blood to the earth.
verses.63:7: I remembered the mercy of the Lord, the excellences of the Lord in all that He repays to us. The Lord is a good judge to the house of Israel; He brings to us according to His mercy and according to the abundance of His righteousness.
verses.63:8: And He said, "Are they not My people? Children, they will certainly not break faith," and He became salvation to them
verses.63:9: out of all their affliction. Not an envoy nor an angel, but He Himself saved them, because He loved them and spared them; He Himself redeemed them and took them up, and exalted them all the days of old.
verses.63:10: But they disobeyed and provoked His Holy Spirit; and He turned to enmity against them, He Himself fought against them.
verses.63:11: And he remembered days of old: Where is the One who brought up from the sea the shepherd of the sheep? Where is the One who put the Holy Spirit within them?
verses.63:12: The One who led Moses by the right hand, the arm of His glory? He overpowered water before him, to make for Himself an everlasting name.
verses.63:13: He led them through the deep like a horse through a wilderness, and they did not grow weary,
verses.63:14: and like cattle through a plain; the Spirit came down from the Lord and guided them. Thus You led Your people, to make for Yourself a name of glory.
verses.63:15: Turn back from heaven and look from Your holy house and Your glory; where is Your zeal and Your strength? Where is the abundance of Your mercy and Your compassions, that You have held back from us?
verses.63:16: For You are our Father, because Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not recognize us; but You, Lord, are our Father; rescue us; from the beginning Your name is upon us.
verses.63:17: Why have You caused us to wander, Lord, from Your way? Have You hardened our hearts so as not to fear You? Turn back for the sake of Your servants, for the sake of the tribes of Your inheritance,
verses.63:18: so that we may inherit a little of Your holy mountain.
verses.63:19: We have become as from the beginning, when You did not rule over us, nor was Your name called upon us. If You open heaven, trembling will seize mountains from You, and they will melt
verses.64:1: as wax melts from fire, and fire will burn up the adversaries, and Your name will be manifest among the adversaries; before Your presence nations will be thrown into turmoil,
verses.64:2: when You do glorious things; trembling will seize mountains from You.
verses.64:3: From ancient times we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen a god besides You, and Your works that You will do for those who wait for mercy.
verses.64:4: He will meet those who do what is right, and they will remember Your ways. Look, You were angry, and we sinned; because of this we went astray,
verses.64:5: and all of us became like unclean ones, all our righteousness is like a rag of a menstruating woman; and we fell away like leaves because of our lawless deeds; so a wind will carry us away.
verses.64:6: And there is no one who calls upon Your name and who remembers to take hold of You; for You have turned Your face away from us, and handed us over because of our sins.
verses.64:7: And now, Lord, You are our Father, and we are clay; all of us are the works of Your hands.
verses.64:8: Do not be greatly angry with us, and do not remember our sins in time; and now look down, for all of us are Your people.
verses.64:9: The city of Your sanctuary became a wilderness, Zion; Jerusalem became like a wilderness; for a curse
verses.64:10: the house, our sanctuary, and the glory that our fathers blessed, became burned with fire, and all our glorious things collapsed.
verses.64:11: And at all these things You held back, Lord, and kept silent, and humbled us greatly.
verses.65:1: I became manifest to those who do not inquire of Me, I was found by those who do not seek Me; I said, "Here I am," to the nation who did not call My name.
verses.65:2: I stretched out My hands all day long to a disobedient and contradicting people, to those who walk in a way that is not good, but after their sins.
verses.65:3: This people is the one who provokes Me before Me continually; they sacrifice in the gardens and burn incense upon the bricks to the demons that do not exist,
verses.65:4: in the tombs and in the caves they sleep for dreams, those who eat pig's flesh and broth of sacrifices—all their vessels are defiled,
verses.65:5: those who say, "Far from me, do not come near me, for I am pure"; this is smoke of My wrath; a fire burns in it all the days.
verses.65:6: Look, it is written before Me: "I will not keep silent until I repay into their bosom
verses.65:7: their sins and those of their fathers," says the Lord; those who burned incense on the mountains and reviled Me on the hills—I will repay their works into their bosom.
verses.65:8: Thus says the Lord, "Just as a grape is found in the cluster, and they say, 'Do not destroy it, for a blessing is in it,' so I will do for the sake of him who serves Me; for this reason I will by no means destroy everyone.
verses.65:9: And I will bring out the seed from Jacob and from Judah, and it will inherit My holy mountain; and My chosen ones and My servants will inherit it, and they will dwell there.
verses.65:10: And in the forest there will be folds for flocks, and the Valley of Achor for a resting place of herds, for My people who sought Me.
verses.65:11: But you who forsake Me and forget My holy mountain, and prepare a table for the demon and fill a mixed drink for Fortune,
verses.65:12: I will hand you over to the sword; all of you will fall in slaughter, because I called you and you did not listen, I spoke and you disregarded, and you did what was evil before Me and chose what I did not desire."
verses.65:13: Therefore thus says the Lord, "Look, those who serve Me will eat, but you will go hungry; look, those who serve Me will drink, but you will be thirsty; look, those who serve Me will be glad, but you will be put to shame;
verses.65:14: look, those who serve Me will exult in gladness, but you will cry out because of pain of heart, and from crushing of your spirit you will wail.
verses.65:15: For you will leave your name for satiety to My chosen ones, and the Lord will put you to death. But for those who serve Me, a new name will be called,
verses.65:16: which will be blessed on the earth; for they will bless the true God, and those who swear on the earth will swear by the true God. For they will forget the former affliction, and it will not come up into their heart.
verses.65:17: For the heaven will be new and the earth new, and they will by no means remember the former things, nor will they ever come upon their heart,
verses.65:18: but gladness and exultation they will find in it; for look, I am making Jerusalem exultation and My people gladness.
verses.65:19: And I will exult over Jerusalem, and I will be glad over My people; and no longer will the sound of weeping or the sound of crying out be heard in her,
verses.65:20: nor will there ever again be there one dying prematurely or an old man who will not fill up his time; for the youth will be a hundred years old, and the sinner dying at a hundred years will also be accursed.
verses.65:21: And they will build houses and they themselves will inhabit them, and they will plant vineyards and they themselves will eat their produce;
verses.65:22: they will by no means build and others inhabit them, and they will by no means plant and others eat. For like the days of the tree of life will be the days of My people; for they will wear out the works of their labors.
verses.65:23: My chosen ones will not toil in vain, nor will they bear children for a curse, because they are a seed blessed by God, and their descendants with them.
verses.65:24: And it will be that before they cry out, I will listen to them; while they are still speaking, I will say, 'What is it?'
verses.65:25: Then wolves and lambs will graze together, and a lion will eat straw like an ox, and a serpent, earth like bread. They will not harm nor destroy upon My holy mountain," says the Lord.
verses.66:1: Thus says the Lord, "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is the footstool of My feet; what sort of house will you build for Me? And what is the place of My rest?
verses.66:2: For My hand made all these things, and all these things are Mine," says the Lord; "and upon whom will I look, except upon the humble and quiet person, and the one who trembles at My words?
verses.66:3: But the lawless one who sacrifices a calf to Me is like one who kills a dog; the one who offers fine flour, like pig's blood; the one who gives frankincense for a memorial, like a blasphemer. And they themselves chose their ways, and their soul desired their abominations,
verses.66:4: and I will receive their mockeries, and I will pay back their sins to them; because I called them and they did not listen to Me, I spoke and they did not hear, and they did what was evil before Me, and chose what I did not desire."
verses.66:5: Hear the words of the Lord, you who tremble at His word: Say, our brothers, to those who hate you and detest you, that the name of the Lord may be glorified and appear in their gladness, and they will be put to shame.
verses.66:6: A sound of outcry from the city, a sound from the temple, a sound of the Lord paying back repayment to those who oppose.
verses.66:7: Before the woman in labor gave birth, before the pain of birth pangs came, she escaped and gave birth to a male child.
verses.66:8: Who has heard such a thing, and who has seen in this way? Has a land been in labor in one day, or has a nation even been born all at once? Because Zion was in labor and gave birth to her children.
verses.66:9: "And I gave this expectation, and you did not remember Me," said the Lord. "Look, did I not make the one who gives birth and the barren woman?" said your God.
verses.66:10: Be glad, Jerusalem, and celebrate a festival in her, all you who love her; rejoice with joy alongside her, all you who mourn over her,
verses.66:11: so that you may nurse and be filled from the breast of her comfort, so that, having nursed fully, you may delight yourselves from the entrance of her glory.
verses.66:12: For thus says the Lord, "Look, I am turning toward them like a river of peace, and like a torrent flooding the glory of the nations; their children will be carried on shoulders and comforted on knees.
verses.66:13: Just as if a mother comforts someone, so I also will comfort you, and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
verses.66:14: And you will see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones will sprout like grass; and the hand of the Lord will be known to those who fear Him, and He will threaten those who disobey."
verses.66:15: For look, the Lord will come like fire, and His chariots like a whirlwind, to repay His vengeance in wrath and His utter rejection in a flame of fire.
verses.66:16: For by the fire of the Lord all the earth will be judged, and by His sword all flesh; many will be wounded by the Lord.
verses.66:17: Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves for the gardens, and in the porches eat pig's flesh and the abominations and the mouse, they will be consumed together, said the Lord.
verses.66:18: And I—their works and their thought; I am coming to gather all the nations and the tongues, and they will come and see My glory.
verses.66:19: And I will leave a sign upon them, and I will send out saved ones from among them to the nations, to Tarshish and Put and Lud and Meshech, and to Tubal and to Greece, and to the distant islands, who have not heard My name nor seen My glory; and they will declare My glory among the nations.
verses.66:20: And they will bring your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the Lord, with horses and chariots, in covered wagons of mules with sunshades, to the holy city Jerusalem, said the Lord, just as the sons of Israel would bring their sacrifices to Me with psalms into the house of the Lord.
verses.66:21: And from them I will take priests and Levites, said the Lord.
verses.66:22: For just as the new heaven and the new earth that I am making remain before Me, says the Lord, so your seed and your name will stand.
verses.66:23: And it will be that month after month and Sabbath after Sabbath, all flesh will come to worship before Me in Jerusalem, said the Lord.
verses.66:24: And they will go out and see the corpses of the people who transgressed against Me; for their worm will not die, and their fire will not be extinguished, and they will be a spectacle to all flesh.

notes.1:1: The Septuagint reads Judea (corresponding to Judah in the Hebrew text), repeats the clause "which he saw," and uses the preposition "against" (kata) rather than "concerning."
notes.1:6: Unlike the Hebrew text ("there is no soundness in it; wounds and bruises..."), the Greek negates all three injury terms ("neither wound nor bruise nor festering blow"), emphasizing either the lack of ordinary treatable injuries or total devastation beneath the surface.
notes.1:9: "Sabaoth" preserves the Septuagint transliteration of the Hebrew title meaning "hosts" or "armies," and "seed" renders Greek sperma, where the Hebrew text reads "survivor."
notes.1:18: "I will make them white" renders the Septuagint first-person singular active verb (leukano) in both clauses, whereas the Hebrew text uses third-person plural ("they will be white" / "will be like wool").
notes.1:27: "Her captivity will be saved, and with mercy" follows the Septuagint (he aichmalosia autes and eleemosynes), differing from the Hebrew text ("Zion will be redeemed with justice, and her repentant ones with righteousness").
notes.2:2: Where the Hebrew text has a single construct phrase ("the mountain of the house of the Lord"), the Septuagint divides it into two parallel subjects: "the mountain of the Lord" (which will be "clearly visible") and "the house of God" ("on the top of the mountains").
notes.2:6: "He has forsaken" translates a third-person verb (unlike the second-person address in Hebrew), and "as from the beginning" interprets Hebrew miqqedem temporally rather than geographically ("from the east"); "foreigners" renders allophyloi, often used in the Septuagint for the Philistines.
notes.2:11: "For the eyes of the Lord are high, while humanity is low" translates the Septuagint's contrast between God and humanity, diverging from the Hebrew text ("The haughty eyes of humanity will be brought low").
notes.2:20: "To the worthless things" renders Greek tois mataiois (futile idols) where the Hebrew text has "to the moles/shrews"; Septuagint Isaiah 2 also ends at verse 21 without the additional verse found at 2:22 in the Hebrew text.
notes.3:1: Sabaoth (σαβαώθ) is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew title meaning 'of hosts/armies,' retained consistently in LXX Isaiah. Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'support and staff,' the LXX renders 'a strong man and a strong woman.'
notes.3:10: The LXX reads 'Let us bind the righteous one, because he is troublesome to us' (echoed in Wisdom 2:12), differing sharply from the Masoretic Text ('Say to the righteous that it will go well with him').
notes.3:22: Laconian (Λακωνικά) refers to fine, sheer Spartan-style garments and is an LXX-distinct geographic designation not present in the Masoretic Text.
notes.3:25: The LXX reads the first clause in the singular ('your most handsome son whom you love'), whereas the Masoretic Text has plural 'your men'; similarly in 3:26, the LXX has 'the cases of your adornment' rather than 'her gates.'
notes.4:2: Instead of the Masoretic Text's 'branch of the Lord,' the LXX reads 'God will shine forth in counsel with glory,' and adds 'to exalt and glorify' before 'what is left of Israel.'
notes.4:4: The LXX includes 'the sons and' alongside 'the daughters of Zion,' where the Masoretic Text mentions only the daughters.
notes.4:5: Reading 'He will come' (ἥξει) rather than 'will create,' and 'with all the glory it will be sheltered' (σκεπασθήσεται) rather than 'over all the glory will be a canopy,' the LXX preserves a distinct prophetic sequence.
notes.5:1: The LXX shifts to first-person 'for my vineyard' (τῷ ἀμπελῶνί μου) in 5:1 and continues with first-person singular verbs in 5:2 ('I put... I planted...'), whereas the Masoretic Text uses the third person in 5:1-2. In 5:2, 'Sorek' (σωρήκ) is a Greek transliteration of a choice red-grape variety.
notes.5:10: For the Masoretic Text's 'homer' and 'ephah' (a ten-to-one yield ratio), the LXX specifies 'six artabas' producing 'three measures,' using Graeco-Egyptian dry measures.
notes.5:17: The LXX reads 'those who were plundered will graze like bulls' and 'of those who have been taken away' (ἀπειλημμένων, from ἀπολαμβάνω), differing markedly from the Masoretic Text ('lambs will graze as in their pasture... waste places of the rich').
notes.5:19: The Greek text spells εἰδῶμεν ('so that we may see'), an itacistic spelling of ἴδωμεν (compare Σειών for Σιών) common in Codex Vaticanus rather than a repetition of 'know' with γνῶμεν.
notes.5:29: The verb ὀργιῶσιν ('they rage,' from ὀργιάω) shifts mid-verse to singular future verbs ('he will seize... roar... cast out'), continuing into 5:30 and portraying the attacking foe collectively as a single predator.
notes.6:1: Greek reads "and the house was full of His glory," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text (MT) refers to the hem of His robe filling the temple.
notes.6:3: Greek Κύριος σαβαώθ (Kyrios Sabaoth) transliterates the Hebrew title "the Lord of hosts" rather than translating it, as also in 6:5, 7:7, and 8:18.
notes.6:4: Greek reads "the lintel was lifted up," whereas the MT reads "the foundations of the thresholds shook."
notes.6:10: Greek uses past indicatives ("has grown calloused ... they closed") where the MT has imperatives.
notes.6:12: Greek adds "after these things" and reads "those who are left will be multiplied on the land" (MT: "the forsaken places are many"), and 6:13 ends without the MT's "holy seed" clause.
notes.7:3: Greek renders the symbolic name Shear-jashub ("A remnant will return") half in translation ("who is left") and half in transliteration ("Jashub," Greek Iasoub).
notes.7:4: Greek ends with "for when the anger of My wrath comes, I will heal again" and begins 7:5 with "the son of Aram," diverging from the MT ("because of the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram").
notes.7:9: Greek transliterates Samaria here as Somoron (unlike Samareias in 8:4) and renders the closing clause "neither will you by any means understand" (MT: "you will not be established").
notes.7:14: Greek renders the noun with the definite article as ἡ παρθένος ("the virgin") and uses second-person singular "you will call" (MT: "she will call"). Pronouns for the child ("His," and "He" in vv. 15-16) are capitalized following traditional messianic reading; Greek makes no case distinction.
notes.7:25: Greek turns the MT's warning ("you will not go there for fear of briars and thorns") into a promise that every plowed mountain will be plowed and fear will not come there.
notes.8:1: Greek uses the genitive "of a new, large [sheet]" (τόμον καινοῦ μεγάλου) and translates the symbolic name Maher-shalal-hash-baz in 8:1 and 8:3 rather than transliterating it; in 8:2, Zechariah's father is Berechiah (MT: Jeberechiah).
notes.8:6: Greek reads "wants to have Rezin and the son of Remaliah as king over you," diverging from the MT ("rejoices in Rezin and the son of Remaliah").
notes.8:11: Greek reads "they refuse the course of the way of this people" and in 8:12 uses "hard" (σκληρόν) where the MT has "conspiracy."
notes.8:14: Greek introduces a condition and negation ("if you are trusting in Him ... you will not encounter Him as a stumbling of a stone"), whereas the MT makes Him a stumbling stone to both houses of Israel.
notes.8:23: Corresponding to 9:1 in Hebrew/English Bibles; Greek begins "Drink this first, act quickly" (MT: "In the former time He brought into contempt") and leaves the participle before the accusative "the seacoast" implied.
notes.9:4: The Septuagint diverges sharply from the Hebrew here, rendering the imagery of bloody battle garments burned in fire as garments amassed by deceit that must be repaid with recompense, so that their owners wish they had been burned instead.
notes.9:5: Whereas the Hebrew gives four compound royal titles and uses present/perfect verbs ('is born... is given'), the Septuagint uses aorists ('was born... was given') and condenses the titles into 'Messenger of Great Counsel,' followed by God's first-person promise of peace and health. Pronouns for the child ('His/Him' here and in v. 6) are capitalized following traditional messianic reading; Greek makes no case distinction.
notes.9:6: 'Sabaoth' transliterates Greek σαβαώθ (from Hebrew ṣĕbāʾôt, 'of hosts/armies'), which the Septuagint of Isaiah regularly leaves untranslated.
notes.9:7: The Septuagint reads 'death' (Θάνατον, reflecting Hebrew deber 'pestilence') where the Masoretic Text reads 'a word' (dābār).
notes.9:11: Where the Hebrew names 'Aram' and 'the Philistines,' the Septuagint has 'Syria' and 'the Greeks,' reflecting later Hellenistic-era geopolitical identification.
notes.10:6: Unlike the Hebrew ('Against a godless nation I send him...'), the Septuagint makes 'My wrath' the object of 'I will send' and has God command 'My people' rather than the Assyrian.
notes.10:9: The Septuagint differs substantially from the Hebrew ('Is not Calno like Carchemish?...'), introducing Babylon, Calneh (Greek Χαλαννή, matching Gen 10:10, where the Hebrew here has Calno), a reference to the tower built there, and Arabia.
notes.10:15: The final clause translates the Septuagint Greek literally ('and is it not so?'), where the Hebrew reads 'not wood.'
notes.10:28: The Septuagint presents distinct place-name forms in vv. 28–31: 'Aggai' (Ἀγγαί, for Hebrew Aiath in v. 28 and Geba in v. 29), 'Megiddo' (Μαγεδώ, for Hebrew Migron), 'the city of Saul' (for Gibeah of Saul in v. 29), 'in Sa' (ἐν Σά, for Laishah in v. 30), 'Madebena' (for Madmenah in v. 31), and 'Gibbir' (for Gebim in v. 31).
notes.10:29: Greek φεύξεται ('will flee') stands at the end of v. 29 with its subject ἡ θυγάτηρ Γαλείμ ('the daughter of Gallim') at the beginning of v. 30, following the Septuagint's clause division rather than the Masoretic verse break.
notes.11:2: Whereas the Hebrew repeats 'fear of the Lord' in both v. 2 and v. 3, the Septuagint renders the first occurrence as 'godliness' (εὐσεβείας) and the second as 'fear of God,' yielding seven distinct spiritual attributes. Pronouns for the shoot of Jesse ('Him/He/His' in vv. 2-5) are capitalized following traditional messianic reading; Greek makes no case distinction.
notes.11:3: Greek δόξα here carries its classical sense of 'appearance' or 'opinion' (rendering Hebrew 'what His eyes see'), and 'will fill Him' translates ἐμπλήσει αὐτόν where the Hebrew has 'His delight.'
notes.11:10: The Septuagint reads 'who rises up to rule nations' and 'in Him nations will hope,' where the Hebrew has 'stands as a signal for the peoples' and 'the nations will seek Him.' Capitalization of 'One,' 'Him,' and 'His' follows traditional messianic reading; Greek makes no case distinction.
notes.11:14: 'Foreigners' translates Greek ἀλλοφύλων (the usual Septuagint term for the Philistines), and 'Idumea' is the Greek form of Edom; the Septuagint also reads 'in ships' and 'will plunder the sea' where the Hebrew has 'on the slope of the Philistines toward the west.'
notes.11:16: The Septuagint reads 'in Egypt' where the Hebrew has 'from Assyria,' just as v. 11 differs in its list by including 'Babylonia,' 'from the rising of the sun,' and 'Arabia.'
notes.12:1: The LXX reads present-tense "I bless You" (Εὐλογῶ σε), contrasting with the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "I will give thanks to You."
notes.12:2: The LXX reads "my God is my Savior" and "my glory and my praise" (with explicit "in Him" and "for me"), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "God is my salvation" and "my strength and my song."
notes.13:2: The LXX translates "bare mountain" as "level mountain" (ὄρους πεδινοῦ) and renders the final clause as an imperative, "open, you rulers," without an object such as "the gates."
notes.13:4: Greek σαβαώθ (Sabaoth) transliterates the Hebrew title meaning "of hosts/armies," preserved untranslated throughout LXX Isaiah.
notes.13:8: The LXX reads οἱ πρέσβεις ("the envoys"), interpreting the Hebrew consonants ṣîrîm as "messengers" rather than "pangs," and uses the rare verb συμφοράζω ("lament together").
notes.13:12: Souphir (Σουφείρ) is the distinctive Septuagint form corresponding to Ophir in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:21: In vv. 21-22, the LXX employs Greek mythological and creature terms ("sirens," "demons," "onocentaurs," and "hedgehogs") to render the desert animals of the Hebrew text.
notes.14:1: Greek γιώρας is a Semitic loanword (from Aramaic gîyōrā / Hebrew gēr) denoting a proselyte or resident alien.
notes.14:6: The LXX divides vv. 6-7 differently from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, rendering "is at rest and quiet" as masculine singular ("He rested confident"), grammatically continuing the Lord as subject from v. 5 (though some interpret it of the oppressor from v. 4).
notes.14:12: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text's second-person address, the LXX shifts to third person ("How the morning star ... has fallen") and reads "who sent to all the nations" for "who laid low the nations."
notes.14:20: The LXX reads first-person "my land" and "my people" (reflecting Israel's lament from v. 4, or God speaking) in place of the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "your land" and "your people."
notes.14:29: Here and in v. 31, the LXX uses οἱ ἀλλόφυλοι ("the foreigners") for the Philistines/Philistia of the Hebrew text; in v. 31, "there is no way to exist" renders the difficult Greek clause οὐκ ἔστιν τοῦ εἶναι.
notes.15:1: The Greek uses the feminine territorial name "Moabitis" (here and in 15:2, 4, 5, 8; 16:7, alongside "Moab") for the land of Moab, omits "Ar," and renders Hebrew qir as "wall."
notes.15:2: The Greek reads "all arms are gashed" (referring to mourning lacerations), whereas the Hebrew text reads "every beard is cut off."
notes.15:4: Reading the Hebrew consonants as "loins" and "will know," the Greek renders "the loins of Moabitis cry out; her soul will know" where the Hebrew has "armed men" and "trembles."
notes.15:7: Instead of the Hebrew statement about carrying wealth over "the brook of the willows," the Greek presents a rhetorical question and a warning that "Arabs" will be brought upon the ravine.
notes.15:9: The Greek again reads "Arabs" and treats the Hebrew nouns for "lion" and "land" as the proper names "Ariel" and "Adama."
notes.16:1: Where the Hebrew speaks of sending a lamb from Sela to Zion, the Greek reads "I will send like creeping things upon the earth" and turns the second clause into a question about Zion being a desolate rock.
notes.16:2: The Greek addresses "Arnon" in the vocative ("on this side, Arnon, further / take counsel" across vv. 2-3), whereas the Hebrew refers to "the fords of the Arnon."
notes.16:6: The Greek reads "I have removed the pride" and "your divination," interpreting the Hebrew term for idle boasts as divination.
notes.16:7: "Deseth" is an LXX-distinct proper name corresponding to Hebrew "Kir-hareseth," and the verse replaces the Hebrew reference to raisin cakes and moaning with concern for its inhabitants and not being ashamed.
notes.16:11: Reading the Hebrew place name Kir-heres as "wall" and the root for "renew," the Greek has "my inward parts you renewed like a wall."
notes.17:3: The Greek ends the Damascus oracle with "you are no better than the sons of Israel and their glory" (for Hebrew "they will be like the glory of the sons of Israel") and transliterates Hebrew sebaoth ("hosts") as "Sabaoth."
notes.17:5: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name "Rephaim" as an adjective ("in a hard ravine"), describing rocky or unyielding terrain.
notes.17:8: The Greek renders Hebrew Asherim (sacred poles) literally as "the trees" and incense altars as "their abominations."
notes.17:9: Where the Hebrew has "the forsaken places of the forest and the summit" (or Horesh and Amir), the Greek reads the gentilic proper names "the Amorites and the Hivites."
notes.17:11: Interpreting the Hebrew words for "sickness" as "inheritance" and "incurable pain" as "like a father of a man," the Greek speaks of inheriting and allotting an inheritance to sons.
notes.18:1: The Greek reads "wings of a land of ships" where the Masoretic Text has "land of whirring wings" (and in 18:2 has "hostages" where the Masoretic Text has "envoys", along with a future indicative "will go" rather than an imperative).
notes.18:3: The Greek uses an aorist passive subjunctive (arthe, "may be lifted up") following hos ("as"), expressing a prophetic wish or condition paired with "it will be audible."
notes.18:7: The Greek retains the untranslated Hebrew title Sabaoth ("hosts" or "armies") rather than translating it, and characterizes the nation as "that hopes" (elpizon) in contrast to "without hope" (anelpiston) in 18:2.
notes.19:5: The Greek reads "will drink the water beside the sea," interpreting the underlying Hebrew verb as "drink" rather than "be dried up."
notes.19:11: Greek "Tanis" is the Hellenistic Egyptian name corresponding to Hebrew "Zoan" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.19:13: Greek "Memphis" corresponds to Hebrew "Noph" in the Masoretic Text, and "have been exalted" reflects a reading of the Hebrew verb as "lifted up" rather than "deceived."
notes.19:18: Greek "asedek" transliterates Hebrew ha-tsedeq ("the righteousness"), reading "City of Asedek" where the Masoretic Text reads "City of Destruction" (or "City of the Sun").
notes.19:25: The Greek applies "My people" to those residing in Egypt and among the Assyrians and identifies "the land, My inheritance" as Israel, differing from the Masoretic Text, which calls Egypt "My people" and Assyria "the work of My hands."
notes.20:1: The Greek preserves the distinct proper names Tanathan (corresponding to the Assyrian military title "Tartan" in Hebrew) and Arna (corresponding to "Sargon" in Hebrew), and spells Ashdod with its standard Greek form Azotus (Ἄζωτος), modernized here to Ashdod.
notes.20:3: The Greek repeats "three years" twice and uses the plural "signs and wonders" where the Masoretic Text has "three years" once with singular "a sign and a portent."
notes.20:4: The Greek literally reads "having the shame of Egypt covered" (kekalymmenous), in contrast to the Masoretic Text's "with buttocks uncovered, the shame of Egypt."
notes.21:2: Greek reads 'the envoys of the Persians' (hoi presbeis ton Person) where the Hebrew MT has 'besiege, O Media,' apparently reading Hebrew sir ('envoy') instead of sur ('besiege').
notes.21:8: Greek uniquely reads 'call Uriah (Oureian) to the lookout post' and 'The Lord said,' whereas the Hebrew MT reads 'and he cried, A lion: upon the watchtower, O Lord, I stand.'
notes.21:10: Greek transliterates Hebrew sebaot ('hosts/armies') as the title 'Sabaoth' (Sabaoth) throughout this section, and addresses 'you who are left behind and you who are in pain' (MT: 'my threshed one and son of my threshing floor').
notes.21:11: Greek identifies the oracle as 'of Idumea' (Edom) rather than MT 'Dumah' and translates 'Guard the battlements' rather than MT 'Watchman, what of the night?'
notes.22:1: Greek reads 'The word (to rhema) of the valley of Zion (Seion),' whereas the Hebrew MT has 'The oracle of the valley of vision.'
notes.22:6: Greek renders the final clause as 'and a gathering of battle-array' (synagoge parataxeos), whereas the Hebrew MT reads 'and Kir uncovered the shield.'
notes.22:12: Greek preserves the double divine title kyrios Kyrios sabaoth ('the Lord, the Lord Sabaoth'), corresponding to Hebrew Adonay YHWH sebaot.
notes.22:15: The Greek spells the treasurer's name Somnas (accusative Σόμναν, corresponding to Σόβνας in 36:3 and Hebrew Shebna, modernized consistently to Shebna) and adds 'into the chamber' (eis to pastophorion).
notes.22:22: Greek reads 'the glory of David' (ten doxan Dauid) where the Hebrew MT has 'the key of the house of David,' and reads 'he will rule, and there will be no one who opposes' where the MT has 'he will open, and none will shut.'
notes.23:1: Throughout this chapter, the Septuagint identifies MT 'Tarshish' with 'Carthage' (Karchedon) and renders MT 'Kittim' with the Greek gentilics 'Citians' (Kitiaioi / Kitieis, inhabitants of Citium in Cyprus).
notes.23:2: Greek names 'Phoenicia' (Phoinikes) where the Hebrew MT has 'Sidon,' and reads 'become like' (homoioi gegonasin) for MT 'be silent.'
notes.23:8: Greek asks 'Surely she is not inferior, or is she not strong?' where the Hebrew MT describes Tyre as 'the bestower of crowns.'
notes.23:17: Greek reads 'restored to the ancient state' instead of MT 'return to her harlot's wages,' and in v. 18 renders MT 'durable clothing' as 'a contribution (symbolen), a memorial before the Lord.'
notes.24:6: The Septuagint reads "will be poor" (ptochoi esontai) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "are scorched" or "diminished."
notes.24:8: The Septuagint reads "the arrogance and wealth of the ungodly" where the Masoretic Text reads "the noise of revelers."
notes.24:14: The Septuagint renders the final clause "the water of the sea will be troubled," differing from the Masoretic Text ("they shout from the sea/west").
notes.24:21: The Septuagint reads "the array [lit. adornment/order] of heaven" for the Hebrew "host of the height" and uses "bring His hand upon" for "punish."
notes.24:23: The Septuagint reads "the brick will melt, and the wall will fall" where the Masoretic Text has "the moon will be confounded and the sun ashamed," reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.25:2: The Septuagint literally reads "fortified cities so that their foundations might not fall," reinterpreting the Hebrew "fortified city into a ruin."
notes.25:6: "Sabaoth" is the Septuagint's Greek transliteration of the Hebrew title meaning "of hosts/armies" (compare Rom 9:29; James 5:4). The Septuagint also lacks "a feast of rich food" here, rendering the feast root in the following clause as "they will drink gladness."
notes.25:8: In contrast to the Masoretic Text ("He will swallow up death forever") and 1 Cor 15:54, the Septuagint makes "death" (ho thanatos) the nominative subject: "Death, having prevailed, swallowed up."
notes.25:9: The Septuagint reads "in our salvation" (te soteria hemon) where the Masoretic Text has "in His salvation."
notes.25:11: The Septuagint diverges sharply from the Masoretic Text ("as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim"), reading "he will relax his hands, just as he himself brought low in order to destroy."
notes.26:3: The Septuagint connects vv. 3-4 with the cognate phrase "with hope they have hoped" (elpidi elpisan), differing from the Masoretic Text's "steadfast of mind You keep in peace."
notes.26:13: The Septuagint reads an imperative addressed to God, "Take possession of us, Lord," where the Masoretic Text reads "Other lords besides You have ruled over us."
notes.26:14: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew "rephaim" (departed shades) as "physicians" (iatroi) and "all remembrance of them" as "every male of them" (pan arsen auton).
notes.26:17: The Septuagint reads "to Your beloved" (to agapeto sou) where the Masoretic Text has "before You, O Lord."
notes.26:19: The Septuagint reads "those in the tombs" instead of the Masoretic Text's "my dead body," and translates the Hebrew "rephaim" as "the ungodly."
notes.27:3: The LXX diverges sharply from the Hebrew MT, reading "I am a fortified city, a city being besieged" where the MT has "I, the Lord, am its keeper."
notes.27:4: The concluding verb (κατακέκαυμαι, "I have been burned up") is punctuated and framed in the LXX as the opening cry of the city's inhabitants, continuing directly into v. 5.
notes.27:8: The second-person pronoun (σύ, "you") is syntactically ambiguous in Greek; in this context it most naturally addresses the hostile adversary who plotted to kill Israel, though some understand it as addressing God regarding His fierce wind or spirit (cf. MT).
notes.27:12: The LXX reads "fence in" (συμφράξει) instead of the MT's "beat out" or "thresh," and names the border city "Rhinocorura" (Ῥινοκορούρων, modern El-Arish) where the MT has "the Brook of Egypt."
notes.28:1: The LXX reads "hired workers of Ephraim" (οἱ μισθωτοὶ Ἐφράιμ) and "drunk without wine" (οἱ μεθύοντες ἄνευ οἴνου), whereas the MT has "drunkards of Ephraim" and "overcome with wine."
notes.28:5: "Sabaoth" (σαβαώθ, also in 28:22, 28:29, 29:6) retains the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew divine title meaning "of hosts" or "of armies."
notes.28:8: The LXX differs substantially from the MT ("all tables are full of vomit and filth"), reading instead "A curse will devour this counsel; for this counsel is on account of greed" (and similarly "afflicted men" in v. 14 instead of "scoffers").
notes.28:16: The double title κύριος Κύριος ("the Lord, the Lord") reflects the Greek literal rendering of the Hebrew Adonai YHWH; unlike NT citations (Rom 9:33; 1 Pet 2:6), LXX Isaiah has no pronoun ("on it" or "on Him") after "the one who believes."
notes.28:20: In vv. 20–21 and 27–28, the LXX departs markedly from the MT, speaking of being "too weak to be gathered together" (v. 20), "a mountain of the ungodly" and "His rottenness" (v. 21), and "cumin will be eaten with bread" followed by God's promise not to be angry forever (vv. 27–28).
notes.29:1: Unlike the MT ("let the feasts go around"), the LXX concludes v. 1 with "you will eat, for you will eat with Moab," and in v. 2 replaces "mourning and lamentation" with "her strength and wealth."
notes.29:13: The LXX differs slightly from NT citations (Matt 15:8–9; Mark 7:6–7) by including "draws near to Me with its mouth" and coordinating "commandments of men and teachings"; in v. 14 it reads "remove" (μεταθεῖναι) where the MT has "deal wonderfully" and "I will hide" (κρύψω) where 1 Cor 1:19 has "I will set aside."
notes.29:17: The LXX treats Χερμέλ (Carmel) as a proper mountain name ("Mount Carmel" and "Carmel") rather than a common noun ("fruitful field").
notes.29:21: The Greek uses a double accusative construction ("make all who reprove in the gates a stumbling block"), diverging from the MT's "lay a snare for him who reproves in the gate."
notes.29:22: The LXX reads "whom He set apart from Abraham" (ὃν ἀφώρισεν ἐξ Ἀβραάμ), where the MT has "who redeemed Abraham."
notes.30:4: Greek Tanis is the Septuagint name corresponding to Hebrew Zoan; the Septuagint also reads "leaders, evil messengers" where the Hebrew text has "his officials are at Zoan and his envoys reach Hanes."
notes.30:15: Greek doubles the divine title as kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord," reflecting Hebrew Adonai YHWH), and reads "When you turn back and groan" rather than the Hebrew "In returning and rest."
notes.30:20: Greek renders the Hebrew term for "your Teacher" as "those who lead you astray" (hoi planōntes se), continuing in 30:21 with the plural exhortation "let us walk in it."
notes.30:29: Rather than a promise of festive song as in the Hebrew text, the Septuagint frames this verse as a rhetorical rebuke questioning their continual feasting and entry into the sanctuary.
notes.30:33: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew phrase involving Topheth as "you will be called to account" and reads "to reign" (basileuein) where the Hebrew text has "for the king."
notes.31:4: Greek Sabaōth (also in 31:5) transliterates the Hebrew title meaning "of hosts" or "of armies"; in the simile, the Septuagint portrays the enemies as defeated and terrified rather than the lion being undaunted.
notes.31:8: Greek uses the singular Assour (Assyria) with masculine singular pronouns and distinguishes between "man" (anēr) and "human being" (anthrōpos).
notes.31:9: Where the Hebrew text speaks of the Lord "whose fire is in Zion, and whose furnace is in Jerusalem," the Septuagint reads "who has seed in Zion and relatives in Jerusalem."
notes.32:2: The Septuagint diverges markedly from the Hebrew text here, speaking of the man hiding his words and appearing in Zion like a glorious rushing river rather than leaders serving as a shelter from wind and storm.
notes.32:14: Where the Hebrew text mentions "hill and watchtower," the Septuagint reads "the villages" (hai kōmai), and portrays abandoned houses leaving behind a city's wealth.
notes.32:15: Greek transliterates Hebrew karmel as "Chermel" in 32:15 (making Chermel the subject that becomes a wilderness), while rendering the same term as "Carmel" in 32:16. Greek πνεῦμα ἀφ᾽ ὑψηλοῦ ("a spirit from on high") is anarthrous and can also be understood as "the Spirit from on high."
notes.32:19: Unlike the Hebrew forecast of destructive hail, the Septuagint promises safety ("if the hail comes down, it will not come upon you") and confidence for those residing in the forests.
notes.33:1: The Septuagint uniquely reads 'like a moth on a garment, so they will be defeated,' differing from the Masoretic Text ('when you finish betraying').
notes.33:5: The Greek critical text punctuates after 'justice' (genitive) so that 'and in righteousness' (dative) carries directly into v. 6 ('by law they will be handed over'), whereas the Masoretic Text joins 'and righteousness' to v. 5.
notes.33:9: The Greek reads 'Galilee' (Galilaia) where the Masoretic Text has 'Bashan,' and renders the preceding phrase as 'Sharon became marshes.'
notes.33:19: Continuing the question from v. 18 ('those being nourished,' vs. MT 'the towers'), the Greek syntax is notably compressed: 'One with whom' refers back to the people, and 'a despised people' stands in the nominative as the subject of the infinitive 'did not hear.'
notes.33:22: The Septuagint renders 'For my God is great; He will not pass me by,' whereas the Masoretic Text refers to 'a majestic ship' that cannot pass through the waters of v. 21.
notes.34:2: Greek 'their number' (ton arithmon auton) translates the Hebrew for 'their host/army' (compare v. 16, 'in number').
notes.34:3: Greek 'will be drenched' (brachesetai) differs from the Masoretic Text ('will melt').
notes.34:6: The Greek uses the Septuagint proper name 'Idumea' (Idoumaia, also in v. 5) for Edom, and spells Bozrah as 'Bosor' (Βοσόρ, rendered with standard English Bozrah as in 63:1).
notes.34:11: Here and in vv. 13-15 the Septuagint renders desert wildlife with terms including 'ibises,' 'sirens' (v. 13), 'demons' (v. 14), 'onocentaurs' (vv. 11, 14), and 'deer' (v. 15), alongside 'a cord of desert surveying.'
notes.34:17: The Greek shifts abruptly to the second-person plural 'you will inherit' (kleronomesete) before returning to third-person plural 'they will rest.'
notes.35:2: The Greek includes 'the desert places of the Jordan' and 'My people,' both absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.35:4: Greek active imperative parakalesate (literally 'comfort,' used reflexively here as 'take comfort' or 'be encouraged') addresses the 'fainthearted in mind' directly, whereas the Masoretic Text reads 'Say to those of anxious heart.'
notes.35:8: The Septuagint adds 'nor will there be an unclean way there' and reads 'the scattered ones' (hoi diesparmenoi) where the Masoretic Text has 'fools.'
notes.35:10: The Septuagint adds 'praise and exultation' and concludes with three nouns and an aorist verb ('pain and sorrow and groaning have fled away'), contrasting with the Masoretic Text's future 'sorrow and sighing shall flee away.'
notes.36:7: LXX omits the second half of the verse found in the Hebrew MT regarding Hezekiah removing the high places and altars.
notes.36:9: LXX diverges markedly from the Hebrew MT, reading 'in the face of the governors' without mention of a captain of the master's servants, and treating 'those who trust in Egypt' as the subject of 'are household servants.'
notes.36:11: Greek 'Syristi' ('in Syrian') refers to Aramaic, and 'Ioudaisti' ('in Judean') refers to the Hebrew dialect spoken in Judea (also in 36:13).
notes.36:16: LXX reads 'if you wish to be blessed' (where MT has 'make peace with me') and 'water from your bronze vessel' (Greek 'tou chalkou hymon'), where MT has 'his cistern.'
notes.36:19: LXX reads 'Epharvaim' (Greek 'Eppharouaim'), an LXX form corresponding to Hebrew Sepharvaim (also in 37:13).
notes.37:4: LXX directs Isaiah to 'pray to your Lord' (anarthrous 'kyrion sou') concerning those who are left, referring to the Lord God named earlier in the verse.
notes.37:12: LXX reads 'Rapheth' and 'in the country of Theemath' where the Hebrew MT has 'Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar'; similarly, 37:13 reads 'Epharvaim, Anag, Ugava' for Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah.
notes.37:16: 'Sabaoth' is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew title meaning 'of hosts' (armies), left untranslated in LXX Isaiah (also in 37:32).
notes.37:25: LXX reads 'I set a bridge, and I laid waste waters and every gathering of water' where MT has 'I dug wells and drank waters, and dried up all the streams of Egypt'; in 37:26, the Greek reads first-person 'ekousa' ('Did I not hear') rather than second-person ('Have you not heard').
notes.37:38: LXX renders 'his god' with 'ton patrarchon autou' ('his ancestral god' or 'patron deity') and reads 'Armenia' where the Hebrew MT has 'the land of Ararat.'
notes.38:1: The Greek spells Isaiah's father Ἀμώς (identical to the prophet Amos), rendered consistently with the standard modern English form Amoz throughout Isaiah.
notes.38:8: The Greek text reads "of the house of your father" where the Hebrew text has "the steps of Ahaz," and describes the sun itself going up the steps after the shadow descended.
notes.38:17: The Greek text reads "behind me all the sins" (ὀπίσω μου πάσας τὰς ἁμαρτίας) rather than the Hebrew "behind Your back all my sins."
notes.38:19: Unlike the Hebrew text ("the father to the children makes known Your faithfulness"), the Greek text has Hezekiah promise to produce children from that day forward who will declare God's righteousness.
notes.38:22: The Greek text renders this verse as a declarative statement naming Hezekiah in the third person rather than a question as in the Hebrew text, and verse 21 omits mention of the boil.
notes.39:1: The Greek text adds "and envoys" (καὶ πρέσβεις) to the items sent by Merodach-baladan, king of Babylonia.
notes.39:2: "Nechotha" transliterates the Greek νεχωθά, which leaves the Hebrew term (nĕkōt, "treasure house" or "spicery") untranslated; the verse also omits the concluding phrase "or in all his realm" found in the Hebrew text.
notes.39:5: "Sabaoth" retains the Greek transliteration σαβαώθ of the Hebrew divine title meaning "of hosts" or "of armies" (compare Rom 9:29; Jas 5:4).
notes.39:6: In the Greek text, "and God said" (εἶπεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς) links forward via ὅτι directly to the prophecy in verse 7, whereas in the Hebrew text "says the Lord" closes verse 6.
notes.40:2: The Greek text explicitly addresses "Priests" (ἱερεῖς), reads "her humiliation" rather than the Hebrew "her hard service," and omits "all" before "her sins."
notes.40:10: The Greek text renders the Hebrew double divine title with repeated κύριος ("the Lord, the Lord") and reads "the arm with authority" (μετὰ κυρίας), omitting "His" and echoing the root of κύριος.
notes.40:15: The Greek text introduces the sentence conditionally with "If" (εἰ) and renders the final clause as "they will be counted as spittle," differing from the Hebrew text.
